parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment uses "2." merely as numbering for the comment point itself, not as a reference to a section or part of the reviewed paper. It mentions generic topics (empirical demonstration, SR-DQN baseline, Mujoco games) but does not name any section, table, figure, or unique part of the paper. As a result, the authors cannot confidently determine which part the comment addresses; identifying the experimental section would only be an educated guess. The comment does clearly specify the issue: the limited number of baselines and games makes the empirical demonstration insufficient, and it raises concern about generalization to other games. Since the referenced part is not explicitly identified and is not obvious, while the specificity requirement is met, the comment is not fully grounded and falls below the top rubric level.
